evidence: Panthi & Abdelfattah, arXiv 2608.19303 (19 Aug 2026). Abstract: 'raise ToolMaze completion from 10.9% to 28.1% across four models'; 'detection outside the mined vocabulary falls to 46%'. Sec 1: 'it never restricts an action, executes a repair, reveals a benchmark fault label, or consults the evaluator'.
correction: Quote is in Sec. 1 (Introduction), not Sec. 3. Alg. 1 = CheckAndReceipt in Sec. 3. Table 2 = frozen paired ToolMaze completion. 46% is same-tool detection, App. G Table 9 (35/76 = 46.1% Flash; 34/75 = 45.3% Pro).

evidence: Zhu et al., arXiv 2606.05806 (4 Jun 2026). Abstract: 'sharpest drops under implicit semantic failures. ...Perturbation Recovery Rate (PRR) plummets by around 37% in these scenarios, while complex topologies trap agents in futile trial-and-error loops.'
correction: Small wording fix: PRR drops by about 37% under implicit semantic failures. The paper does not say PRR equals 37%. Suggested claim: 'Implicit semantic tool failures cause the sharpest degradation; PRR drops by around 37%, driven by over-trust in corrupted outputs.'

evidence: Liu et al., arXiv 2601.04688 (8 Jan 2026). Sec 3.2 defines Hoare-style pre/postcondition contracts. Sec 3.4: 'If verification fails, the result is discarded entirely, preventing contaminated outputs from propagating'. Alg. 1 (App. E) adds failed tools to a per-query failed set and does no repair.
correction: Alg. 1 is in App. E. Table 3 (Sec 5.4) breaks down rejections on MCP-Universe (29.4% total; postcondition 11.8%). The failed set is reset for each query, so nothing persists across runs.

evidence: PyPI verimcp 0.3.0, released 2026-08-15, MIT. Solution: 'transparent proxy that sits between an MCP Host and a backend server'; 'independently re-derive the real outcome (re-read the file, re-check the git log, re-run the safe parts of a CI step)'.
correction: Could add that it rewrites a false success into an error and serves verified retries from cache. It covers only write_file, git_commit/git_branch and run_ci_pipeline.

evidence: Sunny Dubey, arXiv 2608.02464 (3 Aug 2026). Abstract: 'each flagged run is rolled back and re-run live, recovering 45% of failures against a 16% resampling control (p=0.0005) and lifting task success from 52% to 73%'.
correction: 'Tool code is not changed' is our inference from the abstract; the paper does not say it outright.

evidence: Wang, Poskitt, Sun, arXiv 2503.18666 (v1 Mar 2025, v3 Jul 2025), ICSE 2026. Sec 3.1: 'Each rule consists of five parts' (rule, trigger, check, enforce, end). Sec 5.5: parsing about 1.42 ms, predicate evaluation 1.11-2.83 ms, overhead 'on the order of milliseconds'.
correction: Replace the [verify] quote with the verbatim Sec 3.1 'Each rule consists of five parts', or Sec 3.1 trigger = 'the event that activates the rule'. Venue: ICSE 2026 (Proc. ICSE'26, pp. 2938-2950). Table 1 lists monitored events.

evidence: Xiao & Nuzzo, arXiv 2609.18128 (16 Sep 2026). Abstract: LTLf contracts compiled to DFA serving two roles; 'no single deterministic artifact supports both roles'. Sec 6.2 Table 3 (gpt-4o): no defense ASR 47.7%; ContrAgent trace-learned 0.79% at utility 72.6%.
correction: Say that the 47.7% to 0.79% figure is for gpt-4o with the trace-learned variant. Pooled across models, trace-learned ASR is 1.7%, and the variant without a detector reaches 11.1%. Online enforcement uses residual-formula progression.

evidence: Bhardwaj, arXiv 2602.22302 (25 Feb 2026). Abstract: 'C = (P, I, G, R) specifies Preconditions, Invariants, Governance policies, and Recovery mechanisms'. Title footnote: 'Patent pending. Reference implementation and benchmark suite available subject to intellectual property clearance.'
correction: Full title: 'Agent Behavioral Contracts: Formal Specification and Runtime Enforcement for Reliable Autonomous AI Agents'. Single author; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Note that the abstract names the implementation AgentAssert and the benchmark AgentContract-Bench.
